result.summary:
Re-ran `grep -rniE --include="*.md" "hard gate|structurally impossible|Backend gate|Frontend gate" docs/anti-patterns.md` myself and confirmed exactly five real line-matches: 1578, 1611, 1689, 1910, 1920 (matches the validator's independent grep exactly). Opened `docs/anti-patterns.md` at each of the five lines directly and read the surrounding section for each before writing anything:

- Line 1578 ("top-level `status` field" anti-pattern section, first occurrence write-up): "...This was caught only at CI (PR #681's first `Backend gate` run failed on it)..." -- the PR #681 / `lint_handoffs` status-enum incident.
- Line 1611 (same section, later recurrence write-up): "...instead make it structurally impossible (e.g. ORCH greps every handoff it did not itself author...)" -- a proposed future ORCH-side check, not a description of any enforcement that exists today.
- Line 1689 (separate "`mix format --check-formatted`" anti-pattern section): "REQ-167's PR #688 failed CI's backend gate on the very first run..." -- a distinct incident from line 1578 (formatter line-length rejection, not the status-enum mistake).
- Line 1910 (separate "dead default argument" anti-pattern section, REQ-195 recurrence): "...the same narrow ISS-0069-focused task CI's backend gate runs..." -- a third distinct incident, about a compiler warning that only surfaces under a specific mix task.
- Line 1920 (same "dead default argument" section, later REQ-203 recurrence): "...past FIVE separate hard gates that each ran a real `mix compile`/`mix test` pass on this exact file..." -- a different occurrence of the same anti-pattern as line 1910, still describing what got past review gates, not `main`'s git-merge protection.

So the true shape is 5 hits across 3 distinct anti-pattern sections, not 3 hits/3 incidents as previously written: the "status field" section contributes 2 hits (1578, 1611) from its own incident-plus-proposed-future-tooling narrative, the "format --check-formatted" section contributes 1 hit (1689) from a wholly separate incident, and the "dead default argument" section contributes 2 hits (1910, 1920) from two separate recurrences (REQ-195, REQ-203) of that same anti-pattern. Rewrote the Consequences bullet to state "five hits, across three distinct anti-pattern sections" and itemize each of the five lines individually with its section, incident, and quoted text, closing with the same substantive conclusion as before (none of the five asserts a current, general claim about `main`'s merge protection -- they recount past CI/review-gate incidents or propose unrelated future tooling), now grounded in the accurate, complete five-line set rather than a silently-undercounted three.

Verified via `git diff --stat` that exactly one file changed (`docs/migration/decisions/0018-branch-protection-posture.md`) and via `git diff` that the edit is confined to the `docs/anti-patterns.md` bullet inside the Consequences section -- decisions (a)/(b)/(c)/(d), the Step 1-4 command sequences/AC3 verification plan, and the other eight already-passed file characterizations (AGENT_SYSTEM.md/WF-02/WF-01/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md/0014-.../GIT_SETUP.md/0011-.../0017-...) are untouched.
